title: Effects of sauerkraut (from red cabbage) on symptoms of allergic rhinitis, inflammatory markers and the gut microbiome in young adults.
summary:
This study is investigating whether the regular consumption of sauerkraut can alleviate the symptoms of seasonal allergies in young adults. It also examines how sauerkraut affects inflammation levels in the body and the gut microbiome.
Seasonal allergies occur when the immune system reacts hypersensitively to substances from the environment such as pollen or house dust mites. New scientific findings show that the gut microbiome could play an important role in this.
Fermented foods such as sauerkraut contain special ingredients that have an anti-inflammatory effect and can have a positive influence on the immune system. The study aims to clarify whether sauerkraut can be a natural support for allergies and at the same time help to better understand how nutrition, intestinal flora and the immune system interact.

interventions.name:
Daily consumption of a fermented (non-pasteurised) red cabbage product for 8 weeks as follows:
Week 1: 25 g per day
Week 2: 50 g per day
From week 3 to week 8: 75 g per day

Daily consumption of a non-fermented comparative product for 8 weeks as follows:
Week 1: 25 g per day
Week 2: 50 g per day
From week 3 to week 8: 75 g per day

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of seasonal allergic rhinitis and/or conjunctivitis, with a VAS score of >=4 in response to the question: “Thinking back to past allergy seasons, how much did your allergy symptoms bother you when you were not taking medication?” 
- Willingness to consume the predetermined amount of sauerkraut or placebo daily
- Consumption of a maximum of 2 additional portions of other fermented vegetables (whether pasteurized or unpasteurized) per week for at least 4 weeks before the start of the study until the end of the study
- Written informed consent from the participant
Exclusion criteria:
- Presence of a chronic or acute illness other than allergy
- Regular use of the following medications: Antibiotics, antidepressants, immunotherapy, antihistamines, immunomodulatory drugs (corticosteroids, other immune-modifying drugs), emergency medication is permitted
- Pregnant or breastfeeding women
- Intolerance to fermented foods, probiotics or cabbage
- Use of probiotics, prebiotics or postbiotics
- Consumption of 3 or more fermented foods per week within the last 4 weeks before the start of the study
